Lalmohan Babu.description: A writer of detective stories and a recurring companion of Feluda, also known by his pen name Jatayu and sometimes referred to as Mr Ganguli.

Feluda.description: The main detective of the story, renowned for his sharp intellect and investigative skills, whose real name is Prodosh C. Mitter.

Navjeevan Haldar.description: A renowned professor of history invited to Sonahati for a joint reception, commonly referred to as Prof Haldar.

Panchanan Mallik.description: The wealthiest man in Sonahati, president of the Recreation Club, and a collector of antiques.

Someshwar Saha.description: A lawyer and Feluda's old classmate living in Sonahati who hosts the group for dinner; he is sometimes referred to as Mr Saha.

Naresh Sen.description: The secretary of the Sonahati Recreation Club who invited Feluda and Prof Haldar.

Sonahati.description: A town in Bengal, formerly a village, now with modern amenities like a school, hospital, and hotel.

Travelling in Bengal.description: A book Feluda is reading, providing information about Sonahati.

Shiv temple.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in Sonahati.

Mangal Deeghi.description: A large lake in Sonahati, built by a local zamindar.

zamindars.description: Landowners in India, especially during the Mughal and British periods, often wealthy and influential.

Recreation Club.description: A local club in Sonahati that organized the reception for Feluda and Prof Haldar.

Calcutta.description: A major city in India, now known as Kolkata, from where the protagonists travel.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, commonly used by affluent individuals and officials.

Maharshi Debendranath.description: Maharshi Debendranath, often referred to simply as Maharshi, was Rabindranath Tagore’s father and a respected figure in Bengal.

maharaja.description: A Sanskrit title for a great king or prince in India.

jamavar.description: A type of luxurious, intricately woven shawl from Kashmir.

Mr Mallik.description: Refers to Panchanan Mallik, the host and president of the Recreation Club.

kurta.description: A traditional long shirt worn in South Asia, often by men.

achkan.description: A knee-length coat-like garment worn by men in India, usually for formal occasions.

pyjamas.description: Loose-fitting trousers, part of traditional South Asian attire.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or guard, commonly employed for security in India.

sherbet.description: A sweet, flavored drink popular in South Asia, usually served cold.

Jaichand Boral.description: A schoolteacher and descendant of jewellers who is the original owner of the rare pink pearl; sometimes referred to simply as Jaich.

Mrs Saha.description: Someshwar Saha’s wife, who welcomes the guests.

Tipu Sultan.description: A historical ruler of Mysore, known for his resistance against British colonialism.

Robert Clive.description: A British officer and colonial administrator in India during the 18th century.

Siraj-ud-daula.description: The last independent Nawab of Bengal, defeated at the Battle of Plassey.

Rani Rashmoni.description: A philanthropist and founder of the Dakshineswar Kali Temple in Bengal.

Kashmiri.description: Relating to Kashmir, a region in northern India, known for its fine shawls.

Madras.description: A city on the southeastern coast of India, now called Chennai.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, historically significant and culturally rich.

India.description: A South Asian country, setting for the story.

naagra.description: Naagra (or naagras) refers to traditional Indian slip-on shoes, often made of leather and embroidered.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment in India, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

shawl.description: A piece of fabric worn over the shoulders or head, often used for warmth or ceremonial purposes.

Motilal Boral.description: Motilal Boral is a key character involved in the custody of the pink pearl, cousin of Jaichand Boral, and claims a share in the family heirloom; he is sometimes referred to simply as Motilal or Mr Boral.

Suraj Singh.description: A powerful man from Dharampur, Uttar Pradesh, who wishes to buy the pink pearl and is sometimes referred to simply as Singh.

Srinath.description: A servant or helper who brings tea and water to the guests.

Maganlal Meghraj.description: Maganlal Meghraj is the cunning antagonist and a recurring adversary of Feluda, known for his criminal dealings in antiques and art; he sometimes uses the alias Mr Meghraj.

Benaras.description: Also known as Varanasi, a holy city in Uttar Pradesh, India, where Motilal Boral lives.

Dharampur.description: A fictional or lesser-known town in Uttar Pradesh, described as a former princely state.

Uttar Pradesh.description: Uttar Pradesh, often abbreviated as UP, is a large state in northern India and a key setting for the story.

Dharampur Palace.description: The royal residence in Dharampur, associated with Suraj Singh.

Chittaranjan Avenue.description: A prominent street in Kolkata, where Maganlal Meghraj has a house.

Godrej.description: A well-known Indian brand of safes and security products, here referring to a safe used to store the pearl.

Babu.description: A respectful term used in India for men, often as a suffix to names.

Marwari.description: A term for a member of a business community from Rajasthan, often associated with wealth and trade.

Ganga.description: Maganlal's tall and hefty servant who is ordered to search Mr Boral.

Howrah.description: A major railway station in Kolkata, mentioned as the place where Mr Boral arrived by train.

Jogamaya.description: The name of the hotel where Mr Boral stayed after arriving in Howrah.

huzoor.description: A respectful Urdu term meaning 'sir' or 'master', used to address someone of higher status.

paan-masala.description: A flavored chewing mixture of areca nut and spices, popular in India.

paisa.description: A unit of currency in India, equal to one hundredth of a rupee.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A knowledgeable elder whom Feluda consults for information about Suraj Singh.

Aligarh.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, used as a reference point for Dharampur.

Sherlock Holmes.description: A famous fictional detective created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.

Mycroft.description: Sherlock Holmes's elder brother, known for his intellect.

sherwani.description: A long, formal coat-like garment worn by men in South Asia.

mynah.description: A type of bird native to South Asia, known for its ability to mimic sounds.

Dr Bhowmik.description: The family physician who attends to Feluda after he is found unconscious.

Aparesh.description: A friend of Feluda who works at the railway reservations office and assists with travel information.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, a key location in the story's events.

Amritsar Mail.description: A named express train running between Kolkata and northern Indian cities.

Doon Express.description: Another named express train operating in northern India.

American.description: Refers to traders from the United States visiting India in the context of the story.

Indian.description: Refers to people from India, specifically Suraj Singh in this context.

yoga.description: A traditional Indian practice involving physical postures, breathing, and meditation.

bearer.description: Bearer (or bearers) refers to domestic attendants or servants, especially in Indian households or hotels.

Niranjan Chakravarty.description: The manager of the Calcutta Lodge, familiar with Feluda and his companions from a previous stay.

Sunderlal.description: An elderly jeweller called upon by Maganlal to authenticate the pink pearl.

Calcutta Lodge.description: A lodging establishment in Benaras where Feluda and his companions stay.

Vishwanath.description: Refers to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, a famous Hindu temple in Benaras dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, referenced as a place where the characters previously encountered Maganlal.

Tagore.description: Rabindranath Tagore, often referred to simply as Tagore, was a Nobel laureate poet and polymath from Bengal, whose songs and literary works are iconic in Bengali culture.

ghats.description: Stepped embankments leading down to a river, especially on the Ganges in India, used for bathing and religious rituals.

Uncle.description: A common Indian term of address for an older man, used here by Maganlal for Lalmohan Babu.

Manohar.description: Formerly Maganlal's right-hand man, now working with Motilal; described as a wrestler and intelligent.

Namaskar.description: A respectful greeting in Hindi and Bengali, equivalent to 'hello' or 'greetings.'

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and the narrator of the story, affectionately known as Topshe, who serves as his loyal assistant and chronicler.

Shankarprasad.description: Shankarprasad is Suraj Singh’s secretary, tasked with examining the pearl.

Gyan Bapi.description: Gyan Bapi refers to a notable location in Benaras, specifically the area around the Gyanvapi Mosque (Gyan Bapi Masjid), which is a significant meeting place in the story.

Delhi Express.description: Delhi Express is a train service connecting cities, used by the characters to travel to Delhi.

Janpath Hotel.description: Janpath Hotel is a hotel in Delhi where the characters stay during their visit.

Janpath.description: Janpath is a famous road and shopping area in central Delhi.

Taj Hotel.description: Taj Hotel refers to a luxury hotel in Delhi where Suraj Singh is staying.

Tuesday.description: Tuesday is referenced as a day of the week when key events occur.

Wednesday.description: Wednesday is referenced as a day of the week when key events occur.

Thursday.description: Thursday is referenced as a day of the week when key events occur.

American millionaire.description: An American millionaire is mentioned as a potential buyer for the pearl.

ghungrus.description: Small metallic bells worn by classical Indian dancers around their ankles.

harmonium.description: A keyboard instrument popular in Indian music, producing sound by air forced through reeds.

Shabaash.description: A Hindi exclamation meaning 'well done' or 'bravo'.
